title: In ‘The Body,’ Kristina Bogic and Sara Boustany Have Killer Chemistry as Anya and Elise
text:
How 'The Body' Stars Kristina Bogic and Sara Boustany Brought Anya and Elise’s Queer Longing to Life | Teen Vogue Skip to main content Teen Vogue Search Newsletter Menu Menu Menu Fashion Beauty Culture News Lifestyle Shopping Fest Fashion Expand Celebrity Style Sustainability Trending Designer All Fashion Beauty Expand Makeup Skin Hair Nails All Beauty Culture Expand Music Film TV Art Gaming All Culture News Expand Government Immigration History Environment All News Lifestyle Expand Careers Horoscopes Wellness Mental Health Sex and Relationships Voices All Lifestyle Shopping Chevron MORE Fest Video Search Search Newsletter Contact Us About Teen Vogue TV How The Body Stars Kristina Bogic and Sara Boustany Brought Anya and Elise’s Queer Longing to Life
 Bogic and Boustany sat down with Teen Vogue to share how they created the sapphic best-friend duo in Netflix’s new show. By Angelina Mazza November 12, 2026 (L to R) Kristina Bogic as Anya, Sara Boustany as Elise in episode 101 of The Body. Courtesy of Netflix Warning: Spoilers ahead for Netflix’s The Body . 
 Few relationships are as formative, or as fraught, as the homoerotic, codependent bond between two high-school best friends. In The Body , Quinn Shephard’s coming-of-age thriller, a high-school dance team’s antics set off mass hysteria in their town in 2004. For all its exorcisms and near-deaths, the show’s most intimate drama plays out between co-captains Anya Butler (Kristina Bogic) and Elise Zakaria (Sara Boustany). They’re a sapphic Serena and Blair: Catholic-school queen bees who are dying to kiss.
 To cast the pair, Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell scoured dance schools and TikTok, and met with established actors. (Gammell found one of The Body ’s best-known cast members, Sofia Wiley, who plays new recruit Grace, in a TikTok dance video.) Bogic and Boustany, though, were undeniable from their first Zoom read. “You’d be shocked at how much chemistry you can pick up,” Shephard says. “Something comes through in their eyes. You just feel it in your gut.”
 The Body - Season 1. (L to R) Sara Boustany as Elise, Kristina Bogic as Anya in episode 102 of The Body. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Courtesy of Netflix For many in the cast, The Body is their first major role. “It’s a lot of pressure, obviously,” Boustany tells me. But Shephard and Gammell relished working with so many newcomers. “There’s nothing I like more than seeing someone come into themselves as a performer,” Gammell says, “and being part of discovering that together.”
 Teen Vogue spoke with Bogic and Boustany about finding their characters, choreographing their intimacy scenes, and enjoying spirited debates with each other on set. “Being on this scale with Netflix is an adjustment,” Bogic says from Los Angeles, where she and Boustany have joined their castmates for the premiere. “But we're all really proud, and we're here for the ride.”
 Teen Vogue: Sara, you initially auditioned for Anya. Did you ever see yourself playing Elise? Sara Boustany: The casting director, Jennifer [Venditti], called me after the audition and said, “They think you’re Elise.” I weirdly didn’t get why. Elise is so quippy, and her defense mechanism is to be bitchy, which isn’t really me. But I’d only read the pilot (“Slutty God”), and I was so focused on Anya and trying to get on the show. If I’d stopped to think about it for even thirty seconds, I would’ve been like, Oh, yeah. This is a much better direction for me. 
 TV: When did it start to click? SB: At the callback. I read the same scene I’d auditioned with for Anya—the one where Anya and Elise kiss, and Anya’s like, “You can’t kiss me”—but this time as Elise. And it just felt so much better. I remember thinking, I’m not Anya. I’m Elise, definitely. I don’t usually have that kind of confidence when I audition, so I knew this one would hurt if I didn’t get it.
 The Body - Season 1. (L to R) Kristina Bogic as Anya, Sara Boustany as Elise in episode 105 of The Body. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Courtesy of Netflix TV: I was drawn to Anya at first, too. She has this genuine warmth, whereas Elise comes across as a bit of a mean girl. By the end, though, I think everyone wants to be Elise. Kristina Bogic: I wanted Anya to have that warmth. She's a character you could play in so many different ways. Quinn and Gina initially saw her as quite cold, very poised and precise, but I wanted to soften her. She's not your stereotypical b*tchy popular girl. She has an attitude, she's a leader, but she leads with kindness. I wanted to make her feel as real and relatable as possible.
 TV: Do you remember reading together? SB: I read with more than twenty Anyas. I’d never been sicker in my entire life. I was doing these auditions with my nose dripping. It was awful. Kristina was one of the first people I read with, and I remember it feeling electric. She says so much with her eyes, and we really mesh in the way we work together. I mean, I don't think I've fully figured out how I work, but we were always on the same page about what a scene needed and when to talk to the directors.
 TV: So you had a say in things. KB: Yeah, Quinn really encouraged us to speak up. We were constantly making playlists because music is such a huge part of the show. We’d send the directors songs we loved, like, “I think this could be perfect for this scene.” I was texting them all the time with unsolicited ideas.
 SB: I remember pitching them a song, and it ended up happening.
 TV: Which song? KB: It's the one you hear during Elise and Anya's duet at regionals. I was obsessed with Jeff Buckley at the time, and he has an album called Grace, which felt kind of meant to be. Sara and I were playing around with a few songs, and she cut together a two-minute version of “Lover, You Should've Come Over.” Quinn and Gina loved it. And then Ryan Heffington choreographed the dance.
 SB: I love that scene. I was just so happy Anya and Elise were back . We had to make sure that one was perfect.
 The Body - Season 1. (L to R) Sara Boustany as Elise, Kristina Bogic as Anya in episode 106 of The Body. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Courtesy of Netflix TV: We see Anya and Elise become more physically intimate as the season goes on. What was that like to film together? KB: You'd think those scenes with Sara would be daunting, but we actually had a great time. We trusted each other so much, and it was really nice having a set that was mostly women, especially on the creative team. We felt very protected.
 SB: Obviously, Kristina and I had boundaries around what we were comfortable showing, so the choreography had to be specific. Chala [Hunter] , our intimacy coordinator, was always checking in, even from across the room, like, “You good with that?” She had our backs. You need someone like that, especially when it's all so new.
 KB: I couldn't have asked for anything better. I remember running back and forth from the monitors, like, “Can we watch this? Can we see it?”
 The Body - Season 1. Kristina Bogic as Anya in episode 103 of The Body. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Courtesy of Netflix TV: Anya is very much in denial about her feelings for Elise. Why do you think Elise seems more willing to go there? SB: Elise has a better sense of self. That's why Anya makes so many mistakes; she’s too caught up in what other people think. Elise doesn't give a f*ck. I think she probably would've been fine keeping their thing a secret, as long as it was real between them.
 KB: I think Anya can't even let herself go there in her own mind, because once she admits it to herself, it becomes real. And she feels like God is going to punish her for these sins. I also don't think she would've identified with any queer icons from 2004. She would've been like, I don't want to look like that. I don't want to have to act like that. She puts so much value in her hyper-femininity—it's almost like her currency in this world. So she'll find an excuse for anything. With her and Elise, it’s like, this is just what girls do. It's just fun. It's a massage!
 TV: And she’s in denial about what happened with Grace, too. KB: I think Anya wants to tell Elise about it the whole time. There’s just a lot she can’t face yet.
 The Body - Season 1. Sara Boustany as Elise in episode 105 of The Body. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Courtesy of Netflix TV: Sara, do you think Anya should've confided in Elise? SB: Oh my God, that's all she had to do. That’s actually what Kristina and I fought about the most. I'd be like, “I cannot believe you—she—just won't tell her. It's insane to me.” And Kristina would be like, “I'm trying to protect you!” And I'd say, “OK, you tell yourself that.” I honestly feel like Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros) and Elise could've been friends if Anya had let her in.
 KB: We get really passionate about it. I think our directors have a video of us in their office yelling at each other—with love, always with love. We would sit in Quinn and Gina's office and literally dissect our scenes, almost like a mind journal of what each character was going through. It was really important that we never judged our characters, because I think you can totally feel that in a performance. So with everything they did, we made sure we could justify it to ourselves in some twisted way or another.
 SB: You really have to ride and ride for your character until it’s done. And it's funny—we've fully switched. When we watch the show, I feel for Anya, while Kristina's like, “F*ck, this is not OK.”
 KB: I feel so distant from Anya now. There's so much betrayal. I mean, from Elise's perspective, Anya was about to throw her under the bus.
 TV: I go back and forth on that. KB: I don't think she would have. I don't think she'd do that to Steven (Orlando Norman), either. Anya didn't even really throw Lisbeth under the bus, even though she could have. But there's definitely room for her to grow.
 TV: Do you think Elise would help Anya hide a body? KB: I think they’d pretty much do anything for each other.
 SB: You know what? I think Elise would convince her to call the cops. That's truly what would happen. But if Anya were like, “Please,” I think Elise would be like, “OK.” A million percent. That's her lover.
